rationale: Evidence: all 60 development trials across iterations 1 to 4 ended off_track except one oval finish in iteration 4. Max_error sits at about 0.06 to 0.067, the off-track limit, and every run loses the line 1 to 2 times. Iteration 4 was the best (97.2) after shrinking the sensor footprint to 0.008 m and spreading the sensors to +/-0.03 m. The spread itself is likely the problem: with 0.015 m spacing and a 25 mm (0.0125 m half-width) tape, the sensors at +/-0.015 m see no tape when the robot is centred. Only the centre sensor reads, so the signal goes to zero or jumps sharply at the edges, which explains the line losses and the drift to the limit. Changes, one group at a time: (1) Tighten the sensor spacing to 0.008 m (x = -0.016, -0.008, 0, 0.008, 0.016). With the 0.008 m footprint, the two inner sensors sit fully on the tape when centred, so there is always a graded reading across the line. (2) Keep the weights at (-2, -1, 0, 1, 2), kp 1.5, kd 0.6 and base_speed 1.4, since iteration 4 showed these gains are workable and the sensor change is the largest suspected fault. (3) Raise ki from 0.05 to 0.1 so the integral can counter the fixed left/right motor mismatch, which otherwise produces a steady drift toward the edge. Integral is clamped at +/-2, so this stays small. Wheel geometry, mass and body are unchanged. Expected result: fewer line-loss events (target 0 to 1), max_error below 0.06, lower steering_oscillation, and progress above 0.3, with a better chance of completing the oval and s-bend. The slalom is still the hardest track.
